prs.title: fix(bindings): name the NDK C compiler for Android release builds
prs.body:
## What broke

The `v0.26.0` Release & Publish run (34696833375) failed in all four `Build Android` jobs, in `ring`'s build script:

```
error occurred in cc-rs: failed to find tool "aarch64-linux-android-clang": No such file or directory
```

Nothing published: both `release` and `publish-crates` depend on `build-android`.

## Why

0.26.0 added `ring` to the mobile cdylib via the telemetry uploader (`ureq` -> `rustls`). It is the first dependency in the Android build that compiles C, and it does so through cc-rs, which never reads cargo's linker setting. The workflow set only the linker and `AR`. cc-rs probes PATH for a versioned clang and then `<triple>-clang`; `setup-ndk` puts the NDK root on PATH, not the toolchain bin, so every ABI came up empty.

`build-uniffi-android.sh` has the same gap. It does put the toolchain on PATH, so cc-rs's fallback list finds `aarch64-linux-android21-clang` and `x86_64-linux-android21-clang`, but the list names `armv7a-linux-androideabi16-clang` and `i686-linux-android16-clang`, API levels NDK r24+ no longer ship, so the 32-bit ABIs fail locally too.

## Fix

Both paths export `CC_<triple>` and `CXX_<triple>` pointing at the same versioned clang the linker uses. The workflow derives the variable name from the matrix target, so no new matrix fields.

## Verification

Local, NDK r27, the locked cc 1.2.43:

- `ring` alone under the exact CI env (linker + AR, toolchain off PATH): fails with the CI error. With `CC_aarch64_linux_android` set: builds.
- `ring` alone under the script's env (toolchain on PATH) for armv7: fails with `arm-linux-androideabi-clang` not found. With `CC_armv7_linux_androideabi` set: builds.
- Full `cargo build --release --locked --target armv7-linux-androideabi -p offline-protocol-uniffi`: builds, and `check-elf-alignment.py` reports 16 KB PT_LOAD alignment.

A `workflow_dispatch` dry run of the release workflow on this branch (version `0.26.0`) is the CI-side proof; link in the comments.

## After merge

Per the `version-gate` note and CONTRIBUTING, the tag can be deleted and re-pushed because nothing shipped:

```
git tag -d v0.26.0
git push origin :refs/tags/v0.26.0
git tag v0.26.0 <merge commit>
git push origin v0.26.0
```

prs.title: chore(release): 0.26.0
prs.body:
## Summary

Cuts **v0.26.0**. Nothing here changes behaviour: it is the version bump, the
release notes, the 0.25.0 archive, and the corrections found while auditing the
range.

**Minor rather than patch**, decided on public surface: the telemetry sink API
is deleted on every binding (`installTelemetrySink`, `onTelemetry`,
`pollTelemetry`, `uninstallTelemetrySink`, fourteen TypeScript types, the UDL
`TelemetrySink` callback interface and the dictionaries and enums that typed
it, three Python methods), `TelemetryConfig` is reshaped, `enableTelemetry` and
six companion calls are added, `ProtocolError` gains `TelemetryConfigInvalid`
at position 24, `offline-protocol-telemetry-wire` is a new crate, and
`Event::message_failed` / `Event::relay_demoted` change parameter type.

The release itself is two things: the SDK ships its own telemetry (the whole
pipeline from classification to upload lives in the core, and the crates open
their first socket, over TLS with a bundled root set), and delivery survives a
restart (the inbound pending-decryption queue and the deduplicator's seen set
are persisted, two defaults grow to match, a relay-pushed DM is parked, and the
React Native bridges hold inbound message events while nothing can take them).

## Before cutting: nothing compromising on `main`

Scanned before touching anything, because the repository is public.

- `gitleaks` over all 2145 commits of history and over the working tree: no
  credential. Every hit is a public NIP-44 test vector, a lockfile checksum,
  the zero-key address fixture, or the self-signed `interception.invalid` test
  key the uploader's certificate-refusal test uses.
- By name: the two `debug.keystore` files are the stock React Native debug
  keystore (fingerprint `FA:C6:17:45…`), the `.xcode.env` files carry only
  `NODE_BINARY`, `.env.example` holds placeholders, and the demo app's
  telemetry key is the `PASTE_API_KEY_HERE` placeholder.
- By content: no vendor token shape, no private IP, no internal hostname, no
  home path, no real e-mail beyond the export notice and the third-party
  licence authors.

## Related issues

Refs #435, #436, #437, #438.

## Type of change

- [x] `chore` — build, tooling, or dependency changes

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --lib` passes
- [x] `cargo-deny` is satisfied (`advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] Docs / `CHANGELOG.md` updated where relevant
- [x] No new `unsafe` in core crates
- [x] UDL unchanged in this PR, so no binding regeneration; the generated
      bindings embed no version string, which is why a bump does not touch them

Also run: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`, the
three `no_std` targets (`core`, `sealed`, `leaf` on `thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf`),
`scripts/check-license-consistency.sh`, `npx tsc --noEmit` in
`bindings/react-native`, both tool-workspace lockfiles with `--locked`, and a
repo-wide markdown link and anchor check (138 files, zero broken).

## Version files

`[workspace.package].version` and the eleven internal dependencies in
`[workspace.dependencies]`; the four more declared locally in
`offline-protocol-sealed` and `offline-protocol-leaf`; `Cargo.lock` plus the
two tool-workspace lockfiles; `bindings/python/pyproject.toml`; the npm package
and its lockfile; and the three `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` copies. The eleven
previously published crates sit at 0.25.0 on the sparse index and 0.26.0 is
free.

**One thing the tag needs that this PR cannot do:**
`offline-protocol-telemetry-wire` is a new publishable workspace member and its
name is not reserved on crates.io (404 on the sparse index). `cargo workspaces
publish` will try to create it, which needs the registry token to carry the
publish-new scope. Reserve the name, or confirm the scope, before pushing
`v0.26.0`.

## Archive

`docs/changelog/0.25.md` is new (first release of the series), holding the
0.25.0 section with its six `](docs/…)` links rewritten to `](../…)`. The move
was proven lossless by re-extracting the section from `HEAD:CHANGELOG.md`,
applying the same rewrite, and diffing. Both archive tables gain the row.

## Corrections that are not version bumps

Found by auditing the range: every commit since `v0.25.0` against the
`[Unreleased]` section, every number quoted in the release notes and §20
against the constant that sets it (all match), and the version-adjacent prose.

- **`docs/UPGRADING.md` §4 stated the pre-0.26 dedup defaults as current**
  ("Defaults are `1000` and `3600`"), and §8.2 stated the 30-minute pending
  TTL fallback in the present tense. Both now name the 0.26.0 values and point
  at the new §21. `bindings/python/README.md` was the last surface still
  passing `pending_ttl_ms=1_800_000` "as the SDK default", and
  `docs/configuration.md` still explained the default as 30 minutes one
  paragraph under a table that said 24 hours.
- **A `### Documentation` section and a third header paragraph** for the
  release notes. The section covered ADR 0024, the rewritten telemetry guide,
  the threat model's egress section, C12 and the licensing FAQ nowhere; the
  header named nothing from #438, whose default changes and parked pushed
  messages are the runtime surprises of this release for an app that never
  touches telemetry. §21 of the upgrade guide is new for the same reason.
- **Counts that went stale with the eleventh crate.** `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s
  recipe said ten internal-dependency versions and `release.yml`'s gate
  message said eight; both say eleven, which is what the table holds.
- **ADR 0018 and 0019 said "Shipped in: unreleased"** for a data layer that
  shipped in 0.23.0.
- `docs/README.md` counted twenty-three ADRs against twenty-four files.

Two things checked and deliberately left alone: the archived 0.25.0 text
keeps its original punctuation (it is a move, not a rewrite), and the
`[0.26.0]` section keeps the one prose paragraph that sits between two
`### Added` bullets, because it was reviewed in that shape on #435.
